title: SLO declaration and autoremediation signal design for model endpoints
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Define per-endpoint/model SLI taxonomy, concrete SLO targets, cross-region error-budget arithmetic, and a minimal autoremediation signal design that ties circuit-breakers, priority load-shedding, and automated fallback logic together. Outcome: a reproducible SLO declaration format, enforcement rules, and a runbook for on-call that reduces manual emergency interventions for capacity/failure scenarios.
background: We currently have many ad-hoc SLOs defined per product team. This creates inconsistent behavior during regional capacity pressure and makes automated fallback and traffic eviction brittle. Past incidents showed divergence between latency-driven and quality-driven degradation decisions. This ticket consolidates a single engineering-first approach: explicit SLI definitions (latency, availability, quality), error-budget math for multi-region aggregation, and deterministic autoremediation triggers that play well with dedicated capacity and Redwood's smart routing.
goals: Create a canonical SLO declaration JSON schema for endpoints and model variants
Define 3 core SLIs with measurement guidance: latency (P95/P99), availability (success rate), and semantic quality (eval-set pass rate)
Specify error budget burning arithmetic for per-endpoint + global aggregation across regions
Design deterministic circuit-breaker triggers and automated remediation actions (fallback, throttling, KV cache warming)
Provide on-call runbook and observability dashboards to operationalize enforcement
sli_definitions: Latency: measured as request->final-token P95 and P99 for non-streaming routes; for streaming routes measure first-byte latency P95 and token-emit-rate degradation. Use service side timestamps and normalize to client-visible time windows.

Availability: successful-response rate where success excludes 5xx, 429, and protocol-level interruptions. Calculate as successful_requests / (successful_requests + failed_requests) on a rolling 5m and 1h window.

Quality: measured as proportion of responses that pass a curated prompt-based evaluative test (canary prompts + customer-critical prompt sets). Initially sampled 1% of traffic; metric computed hourly and smoothed with an EWMA to reduce noise.
slo_targets: Latency SLO (P95): 95% of requests under 700ms for 'low-latency' class endpoints; 90% under 1.5s for 'batch' class
Latency SLO (P99): 99% of requests under 3.5s for low-latency routes
Availability SLO: 99.95% over 30d for production endpoints (tiered by customer plan)
Quality SLO: 98% pass rate on the golden prompt set, with rolling regession detection at >2% drop over 24h
error_budget_policy: Error budgets are computed per endpoint-model-variant in tokens-equivalent units: weighted combination of availability and latency budget. We convert a 30d availability target into a token-budget using the endpoint's historical tokens-per-request. For multi-region aggregation, we treat regions as siblings with a soft-reservation (20% of capacity held) and allow borrowing using a lease mechanism: region A may borrow region B's error budget up to 10% of B's daily budget with automated debt repayment policy within 72 hours or trigger conservative global throttles. When an endpoint's error-budget burn rate exceeds 3x expected, automated remediation flows (circuit-breaker) start after a 5-minute verification window.
circuit_breaker_triggers: Immediate open if 5xx rate > 1.0% AND P99 latency > 2x SLO over a 5 minute sliding window
Open if error-budget burn rate > 5x over a 30 minute window (to protect regional reserve)
Soft-open (apply progressive throttles) if sustained elevated queue-length (>75th percentile) and downstream model queue latency increase observed
Recovery: move to half-open after 10 minutes with 10% of traffic for validation, full close once 30 consecutive 1-minute windows are within SLO
load_shedding_policy: Tenant-aware priority eviction: label traffic by customer tier and route class. During eviction, preserve 'critical' tokens (control-plane, paid tier, latency-sensitive) and shed 'best-effort' (background embedding/async batch). Eviction steps: 1) graceful request rejection with informative 429 and reason header; 2) route to cheaper model variant (if allowed by contract) with content-attenuation header; 3) last resort: deny non-critical requests. All shedding decisions must be logged with token counts and approximate lost revenue estimate for postmortem.
multi_region_failover: Prefer warm-standby regions with pre-warmed KV caches and pinned model variants for fast failover
Failover decision priority: local retries -> same-region fallback model -> region-level borrow -> cross-region reroute based on latency/cost policy
Automated failover will only perform cross-region reroute if (a) regional error-budget is exhausted AND (b) customer SLA allows cross-region processing; otherwise notify sales/CS on the issue
observability_and_alerting: Dashboards per endpoint showing SLI time series (P95/P99 latency, success rate, quality pass rate), error-budget remaining, and borrow/debt status
Alerts: SLO burn rate > 2x (P1), 5xx spikes > threshold (P0), failed automated remediation attempts (P1)
Tracing hooks to map slow requests to model variant, kernel selection, and batching group for debugging regressions
rollout_and_enforcement: Phase 1 (canary): apply SLO schema + metrics to 10 internal endpoints, validate noise characteristics and quality metric sampling (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (pilot): expand to 50 customer-facing endpoints and enable autoremediation in simulation mode (alerts only) (4 weeks)
Phase 3: enable active remediation with a 2-hour human-preview window before global cross-region borrow for enterprise-only customers, full-enforcement for non-enterprise after 8 weeks
Enforcement via a controller in routing plane that consumes SLO declarations and evaluates circuit-breaker state every 10s
acceptance_criteria: SLO declaration schema merged and validated by unit tests
Controller can read SLOs and surface SLI metrics to the dashboard for the canary endpoints
Automated remediation triggers simulate without dropping production traffic (alerts-only) and produce reproducible runbook steps
Runbook reviewed and signed-off by on-call and product (Marta)
